subject: Lumina POC onramp: evaluation checklist & GPU scheduling
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lynch <sam.lynch@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Alexandra Rao <alex@luminahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Lumina POC onramp: evaluation checklist & GPU scheduling

Hi Sam / Alex —

Thanks again for the demo earlier — good to align on goals. Per our discovery, I wanted to send a concise recap and an initial runbook for the 3-week POC so we can lock in resources this week. Please review and confirm where noted.

High-level success criteria (we captured on the call):
- 95th pct latency < 600ms for 1k concurrent infer requests (chat-style traffic)
- Response quality: >85% pass rate on Lumina clinical intent eval set (you shared ~5k labeled samples)
- Cost target: average token cost <= $0.0009 per token across evaluation window

Immediate asks for Lumina:
1) Share the eval payload (anonymized) by EOD Wed — filename suggestion: Lumina_eval_set_v1.csv (we have stubbed column mapping in the Drive).
2) Confirm any PII/data handling restrictions we should enforce in the private workspace (HIPAA constraints noted on the call).
3) Approve tentative POC start window: Jun 22 — Jul 10 (3 weeks).

Capacity proposal (preliminary, see attachment POC_capacity_proposal.xlsx):
- Reserved baseline: 2x A100 equivalent GPUs (steady-state) to hit latency SLO for interactive evals.
- Autoscale/burst: allow burst to 6 GPUs for short windows (2–10 min) during batch runs or peak replay traffic; burst uses pre-negotiated pool credits to avoid cold start delays.
- KV-cache warmup: we recommend a 1-hour warmup run with a small traffic replay ahead of formal evals.

Ownership & next steps:
- Redwood: marissa@redwood will coordinate onboarding, infra config, and monitoring dashboards.
- Infra/ops lead: ben@redwood to confirm GPU procurement and autoscale knob settings.
- Evaluation owner: alex@luminahealth to confirm dataset and acceptance tests.

Attachments: POC_MoM.pdf (call minutes), Lumina_eval_set_v1.csv (sample expected format), POC_capacity_proposal.xlsx

If this looks good I’ll loop in ben and karthik to lock dates and run the capacity reservation.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0123

Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2026 11:04:00 -0700

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. We can get you an anonymized slice of the eval set by Wednesday; I’ll ask DataOps to scrub PHI. Confirming HIPAA applies and we’ll provide a signed BAA addendum this week.

A couple clarifications: 
- The 1k concurrent target is peak across our internal testers, but average concurrent is closer to 200. We can provide traffic traces if that helps sizing.
- For quality acceptance, we’ll run blind evals followed by a manual review; target 85% pass is fine to start but we’ll discuss thresholds if we see systematic mismatches.

I’m ok with the Jun 22 start — please loop in your infra team to lock GPU windows; we’d prefer minimal downtime during our working hours (PST).

Sam
Director of Product, Lumina Health
sam.lynch@luminahealth.com

-----Original Message-----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Lynch <sam.lynch@luminahealth.com>, Alexandra Rao <alex@luminahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Lumina POC onramp: evaluation checklist & GPU scheduling

Ben / Karthik / Laura —

Looping you in to convert the discovery recap into an actionable infra plan. Key asks below; open items marked with ACTION.

Proposed infra baseline (to provision this week):
- 2x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved) for Jun 22 — Jul 10 (3 weeks).
- Burst pool: +4 GPUs available for autoscale up to 6 total; policy: burst windows allowed during 07:00–19:00 PST, capped to 30 cumulative minutes/hour per customer.
- Warmup: schedule a 1-hour warmup replay on Jun 21 morning (ACTION: schedule slot and confirm job config).
- Networking: private VPC peering with Lumina (they require traffic over dedicated link). (ACTION: share VPC CIDRs and firewall rules).

Cost notes (estimate):
- Baseline reservation: $X,XXX/week (will provide firm quote once sizing is finalized).
- Burst credit usage billed separately; we can cap spend and notify on threshold.

ACTION ITEMS:
- Ben: confirm availability of 2 reserved A100 equivalents and the burst pool by EOD Thu Jun 10 and attach the exact SKU/pricing to this thread.
- Karthik: prepare canary rollout plan and an automatic fallback to a smaller model if we miss latency SLOs during peak windows.
- Laura: coordinate the VPC peering checklist with Lumina’s network team and produce the short network playbook.

Ben — please add any infra risks you see. I’ll compile and send Lumina the firm reservation notice once you confirm.

Best,
Marissa

-----Original Message-----
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Lumina POC onramp: evaluation checklist & GPU scheduling

Marissa —

Confirming resource availability: we can commit 2x A100-equivalent reservations for the Jun 22 start. Burst pool of +4 GPUs is feasible using our shared burst credits, with the proposed policy window. I’ll attach the SKUs and the rough cost bands in the POC_capacity_proposal.xlsx (uploaded to the Drive link).

Risks / notes:
- If the warmup replay hits different sequence-length distribution than expected, tail latency could spike; recommend we run a small replay with sampled traffic first (15–30 min) to validate cache hit rates.
- Network peering needs the Lumina NOC to confirm CIDR ranges; if we can’t get peering in time, we can fall back to an encrypted transit link, but that adds ~24 hours to setup.

Next steps I’ll take:
1) Finalize SKU and pricing and post to Drive (today).
2) Reserve the GPUs in the reservation system (pending Lumina ack).
3) Pre-create canary image with a smaller model so Karthik can test automatic fallback logic.

Ben Carter
